en.title: Resident Evil: Zach Cregger Strips Out Jokes for Scarier Reboot
en.summary: Filmmaker Zach Cregger reveals a pivotal decision made during test screenings for his upcoming Resident Evil film. By removing humor, Cregger found both audiences and himself more satisfied with the horror experience.
en.body:
When bringing the iconic **Resident Evil** franchise back to the big screen, director **Zach Cregger** faced a common challenge: finding the right tone. Early reactions to his film indicated a strong audience connection, but with a surprising caveat – it was perceived as *too* funny. Cregger's response? A strategic culling of comedic elements, a move that ultimately elevated the film for everyone involved.

## The Cregger Cut: Humor Removed, Horror Amplified

**Zach Cregger** has openly discussed the adjustments made to his **Resident Evil** film following initial test screenings. The feedback was clear: while the movie resonated, its humorous undertones detracted from the intended terror. "I learned that people really liked the movie, but they thought it was too funny," Cregger shared. "So over the course of my testing, I stripped out as much of the jokes as possible." This deliberate pruning wasn't just about appeasing test audiences; Cregger himself found the revised cut to be a significant improvement. "I then found that not only did the audience enjoy the movie more, but I also liked the movie a lot more. A little bit of humor goes a long way in a horror movie, and there’s not a single joke I took out of this movie that I miss."

This approach signals a commitment to delivering a pure horror experience, leaning into the atmospheric dread and visceral scares that have defined the **Resident Evil** games for decades. While Cregger's previous work, like **Barbarian**, showcased his knack for blending genres, this adjustment suggests a more focused vision for his take on the zombie apocalypse. The film is slated for release on September 18, 2026, and is expected to follow a character on a harrowing night in Raccoon City, encountering familiar horrors from the game series.

## A New Direction for Raccoon City

Fans of the **Resident Evil** universe have long debated the perfect balance between action, horror, and even the occasional campy humor that has characterized various entries in the franchise. Cregger's decision to dial back the laughs suggests a return to the franchise's darker roots, potentially resonating with players who prefer the more suspenseful and terrifying aspects of the games. The emphasis on a serious tone could also be a strategic move to differentiate this reboot from previous film adaptations, many of which leaned heavily into action-hero tropes and over-the-top set pieces.

This directorial choice is particularly interesting given the evolving landscape of horror filmmaking and game adaptations. Cregger's willingness to dramatically alter the film based on audience reception, rather than sticking to an initial comedic vision, speaks volumes about his dedication to crafting the most effective horror experience possible. It’s a bold move that prioritizes genuine scares over easy laughs, a gamble that could pay off handsomely for fans eager for a more faithful and frightening interpretation of the **Resident Evil** world.

## What's Next

With **Resident Evil** set to launch on September 18, 2026, **Zach Cregger** has expressed interest in developing sequels, though he plans to tackle another project before returning to the franchise. Further details regarding the cast and specific plot points are expected to be revealed closer to the release date.
